=== 2026-02-19 ===
Midnight 12.0.1 AddOn Restrictions Update

Hello again from Blizzard! We have a small list of changes that are being hotfixed to live in preparation for Early Access launch next week. You should expect these to hit live servers in the next few days.

DISCLAIMER: These notes are for addon authors and as such are focused specifically on addon security changes only. Changes planned for other parts of the game (UI or otherwise) are not included here.

NOTE: While most of these are bugfixes that last couple changes were made to address exploits or addon functionality we did not want to allow. Apologies for the late changes there!


=== Changes due to be deployed before Midnight Early Access ===
*Fixed an exploit that allowed addons to declassify spell names using tricky string formatting. APIs no longer accept secret spell names from addons as a result. (Already live)
*Fixed an exploit where status bars could be used to launder secret numbers.
*Fixed an issue where calling debuglocals after certain Lua errors would cause a crash.
*Fixed an issue where numerous APIs that accept aura instance IDs would stop working after a full aura update (relog was the easiest repro).
*Fixed an issue where enabling timestamps on chat frames would cause Lua errors when chat lockdowns are in effect.
*Threat APIs now conditionally return secrets for some combinations of input unit tokens to prevent unintended use of these functions to compare units.
*Various APIs no longer accept compound unit tokens or unit names when in an active PvP match.
Bonus notes that were forgotten:
Fixed an exploit that allowed addons to access spell IDs and durations of crowd control effects for other players.
Fixed an exploit that allowed addons to access cooldowns of PvP trinkets for other players in arenas.


=== 2026-02-24 ===
Midnight 12.0.1 Spell Declassification Update

Hello again from Blizzard!

Today we have an update regarding which spells we are going to be flagging as non-secret for Midnight launch. These changes are planned to go out in a data hotfix in the next couple days, but we wanted to give you all a heads up beforehand so you can plan any necessary changes to your addons.

Over the course of Beta, as well as recent weeks on live, one of the biggest recurring points of feedback has been from healers who wish that our default UI provided more robust options for filtering or emphasizing specific buffs on raid frames. In the past month we have added a few layers of extra logic to buff sorting and visibility, and while we've heard positive feedback from many healers about these improvements, we realize that our solutions are leaving others still wanting more customization.

While we had originally hoped to be able to deliver a streamlined default experience, it has become clear that there are common use-cases that a single set of logic cannot cover. Some players may want to make simple tweaks like highlighting the target of their Preservation Evoker's Echo, or their Holy Paladin's active Beacon, while others would consider that to be distracting clutter. We are now beginning work on a system to allow players to hide or emphasize buffs from their spellcasts on a per-spell basis, via the Spellbook. We expect that solution to be ready for players in a later Midnight patch.
In the meantime, we have also seen a few addons popping up that use non-secret information to make very reliable guesses about players' spellcasts in order to drive this sort of filtering logic. Breaking the API calls driving this functionality would cause significant collateral damage to common addons, and we are not planning to do go down that path. Ultimately, this design space is mostly about customizing the display of information, rather than objectively advantageous computational solutions, so we want to treat it the same way we approached resources like Holy Power or Maelstrom.

Thus, rather than requiring addon developers to jump through hoops to support an implementation that will have some frustrating inaccuracies, we are planning to flag a number of short-cooldown rotational healer spells, and very long duration buffs, to exclude them from our Secret Value system. We will likely re-protect these spells once our own filtering solution, with its own addon hooks for display customization, is in place.

The full list of spells being flagged is below, broken down into several categories.

=== 2026-03-21 ===
Midnight 12.0.1 Upcoming Restriction Changes

Hello again from Blizzard! Mythic raids and M+ open this week and we will be hotfixing in some last-minute changes to fix exploits before resets.

We recognize that some of these changes are going to be disruptive and require last-second changes to your addons, and we sincerely apologize for them coming in so late. Part of these changes involve removing the secure delegate portion of ActionButton_ApplyCooldown. We have added new APIs that should replace the functionality it provided, but we will be watching closely for reports of functionality that still needs replacing.

DISCLAIMER: These notes are for addon authors and as such are focused specifically on addon security changes only. Changes planned for other parts of the game (UI or otherwise) are not included here.


=== Cooldowns ===
* Removed the ability for tainted code to configure cooldown frames with secret values via Cooldown:SetCooldown, Cooldown:SetCooldownFromExpirationTime, Cooldown:SetCooldownDuration, and Cooldown:SetCooldownUNIX.
** This does not impact Cooldown:SetCooldownFromDurationObject which, going forward, is the only way to configure a cooldown frame with secret values.

* The ActionButton_ApplyCooldown Lua function no longer routes through a secure delegate.

Midnight 12.0.1 Spell Declassification Update

Hello again from Blizzard!

Over the course of Beta, as well as recent weeks on live, one of the biggest recurring points of feedback has been from healers who wish that our default UI provided more robust options for filtering or emphasizing specific buffs on raid frames. In the past month we have added a few layers of extra logic to buff sorting and visibility, and while we've heard positive feedback from many healers about these improvements, we realize that our solutions are leaving others still wanting more customization.

While we had originally hoped to be able to deliver a streamlined default experience, it has become clear that there are common use-cases that a single set of logic cannot cover. Some players may want to make simple tweaks like highlighting the target of their Preservation Evoker's Echo, or their Holy Paladin's active Beacon, while others would consider that to be distracting clutter. === 2026-03-12 ===
Midnight 12.0.5 PTR Changes Episode 1: The Secret Menace

Hello again from Blizzard! With 12.0.5 PTR slated to start today, here is the list of addon API changes you can expect to see in next couple builds, followed by a discussion about some longer-term changes we are considering for the aura system.

DISCLAIMER: These notes are for addon authors and as such are focused specifically on addon security changes only. Changes planned for other parts of the game (UI or otherwise) are not included here.


=== Coming in 12.0.5 PTR 1 ===
=== Numeric Formatting ===
*We have added three new Lua object types for numeric formatting: AbbreviatedNumberFormatter, NumericRuleFormatter, and SecondsFormatter. These types can be supplied with secret numbers through the Format functions on duration objects.
*We're considering adjusting the various "display count" APIs (eg. C_Spell.GetSpellDisplayCount) to accept formatter objects, but this would be a breaking change (let us know your thoughts).

=== Spell & Item Charge APIs ===
*The following APIs will now return a zero-span duration object when the queried spell is at maximum charges: C_SpellBook.GetSpellBookItemChargeDuration, C_Spell.GetSpellChargeDuration, C_ActionBar.GetActionChargeDuration.

=== Duration Objects ===
*DurationObject objects that measure a zero-span are now considered fully elapsed.

=== Auras ===
*The isHelpful, isHarmful, isRaid, isNameplateOnly, and isFromPlayerOrPlayerPet booleans on aura data tables are no longer secret.

=== Transmog ===
*Added GetTransmogOutfitIndex to the restricted environment. Values returned from this can be used with the new /outfit slash command.

=== Lua Documentation ===
*Added a new Predicates table to out Lua API documentation, which will provide a description of the restrictions on each API.

=== Misc. ===
*The Ambiguate function now accepts secrets from addons.
*Added a Cooldown:SetCountdownMillisecondsThreshold(seconds) API. When a cooldown frame is rendering a time below this number of seconds, it will be displayed as a decimal value with one decimal place (e.g. "8.7").
*String formatting APIs no longer honor field width modifiers for secret string values (e.g. the "%.5s" format will no longer truncate a secret string).
*The UnitSpellTargetName API now only returns names for player units.

=== Bug fixes ===
The C_EncounterEvents.GetEventSound API no longer errors when called.


=== Coming in upcoming 12.0.5 PTRs ===
=== Misc. ===
*The UnitTokenFromGUID API (and various others) will no longer return arena, nameplate, boss, party, raid, or target-of-target unit tokens when unit identities are secret.
*UnitTokenNamePlate APIs will no longer accept party, raid, or target-of-target unit tokens.
*Addon execution throttles will no longer apply while the PLAYER_LOGOUT and ADDONS_UNLOADING events are being processed.


=== Future Plans ===

While we have a variety of plans for future patches (12.0.7 and beyond), including many more quality-of-life fixes for addon developers, we wanted to take a moment to talk about one area in particular that we are putting a lot of thought into: Auras (particularly of the Private variety).

We created the Private Aura system back in 10.1 as a means to prevent addons from automating certain very specific fight mechanics. In some ways Private Auras can be viewed as the beginning of our experimentation with adjusting addon capabilities, and while they certainly had their issues, for the most part they served their purpose (albeit in a rather heavy-handed way). When we started developing the Secret Value system, we had hoped (planned even) to be able to essentially retire the Private Aura system and replace it with just secrets.

Unfortunately, as Midnight Alpha & Beta progressed it became clear that relying on Secret Values alone was not going to be enough to prevent addon automation involving auras. And so, we ended up having to go in almost the exact opposite direction: we made MOST encounter debuffs private auras rather than just a select few. While this approach gave us the security we needed for Midnight Season 1, it also came with some significant downsides. Our own private aura displays don't currently have full parity with normal auras, and they aren’t supported in nameplates. On top of that they also require our encounter designers to be very diligent about flagging almost every encounter debuff as private, which is cumbersome and very easy to get wrong.

All this is to say that we are not happy with the current state of auras as they pertain to addons, and we are planning to make some large changes to them. We don't have a hard target yet for when this rework will happen, but just to ease your minds a little it definitely will NOT be in 12.0.5 or 12.0.7. What shape this new aura system will take is also nowhere near decided yet so we won't have any specifics for a while yet, but the overarching goals can be summed up as:

* Auras need to be more secure than they currently are (with less upkeep for designers).
* Auras still need to be customizable and displayable by addons.
* And then as a bonus goal we would like auras to be more performant for addons.

We will be consulting with addon developers as we start to plan out work on this new system, so don't worry about this being dropped on you out of the blue. We just wanted to give you an idea of where our heads are at, so it doesn't come as a surprise later.

Oh and just to make Meo happy, Jar Jar would like to say: Wesa will have mooie tings to share berry soon!



=== 2026-03-25 ===
Midnight 12.0.5 PTR Changes Episode 2: Attack of the Secrets

Hello again from Blizzard! Below you will find a list of changes we have made to addon restriction APIs in the last two 12.0.5 PTR builds, followed by the changes we plan to make in next week's PTR build. We begin with a few changes we will be hotfixing to live.

DISCLAIMER: These notes are for addon authors and as such are focused specifically on addon security changes only. Changes planned for other parts of the game (UI or otherwise) are not included here.


=== Changes being Hotfixed to 12.0.1 ===
* The following APIs will no longer be able to be called by addons during combat: C_PartyInfo.PromoteToLeader, C_PartyInfo.PromoteToAssistant, C_PartyInfo.DemoteAssistant, C_PartyInfo.SetEveryoneIsAssistant, C_PartyInfo.DoReadyCheck, C_PartyInfo.ConfirmReadyCheck, C_PartyInfo.ConvertToParty, C_PartyInfo.ConvertToRaid, C_PartyInfo.ConfirmConvertToRaid, C_PartyInfo.DoCountdown, C_PartyInfo.SetRestrictPings, C_PartyInfo.SetLootMethod.
* Text lines in tooltips that contain secret text will no longer remain secret permanently.
* Fixing a bug where some players randomly become unable to set raid markers until they restart their client.


=== Changes in 12.0.5 PTR 2 and 3 ===
=== Nameplate HitRect APIs ===
* Added an API to allow addons to override the offsets of nameplate hit-rects.

=== UnitToken APIs ===
* The UnitTokenFromGUID API (and various others) no longer return arena, nameplate, boss, party, raid, or target-of-target unit tokens when unit identities are secret.
* UnitTokenNamePlate APIs no longer accept party, raid, or target-of-target unit tokens.

=== UnitIsUnit API ===
* UnitIsUnit now returns secrets if either unit in the comparison is "targettarget" or "focustarget".

=== Misc ===
* Added new FontString:GetSmoothScaling/FontString:SetSmoothScaling APIs to font string objects (XML attributes were added for this back in 12.0.0).

=== Changes coming in 12.0.5 PTR 4 ===
=== UnitIsUnit API ===
* The UnitIsUnit API is being adjusted to apply the following rules:
** If either unit is one of the following, the comparison is permitted: "player", "pet", "vehicle", "mouseover", "target", "softenemy", "softfriend", "softinteract", "focus", "none", "npc", "questnpc"
** If either unit is a party/raid token (or a pet of one) and the other is NOT a compound unit token ("boss1target"), nameplate token, or "targettarget"/"focustarget", the comparison is permitted.
** All other comparisons are disallowed and return nil.

* We are adding a new UnitHasPowerType API that returns a non-secret bool indicating if the unit uses a power type.
* We are adding a new ignoreGCD parameter to APIs that construct and return duration objects for cooldowns.
* We are adding numeric formatter support for Cooldown frame fontstrings.
* We are removing the restrictions that we recently placed on the C_UnitAuras.AddPrivateAuraAnchor, C_UnitAuras.RemovePrivateAuraAnchor and C_UnitAuras.SetPrivateWarningTextAnchor APIs.
** Existing restrictions will remain on the C_UnitAuras.AddPrivateAuraAppliedSound and C_UnitAuras.RemovePrivateAuraAppliedSound APIs.

=== Bug fixes ===

Midnight 12.0.5 PTR Changes Episode 1: The Secret Menace

Hello again from Blizzard! With 12.0.5 PTR slated to start today, here is the list of addon API changes you can expect to see in next couple builds, followed by a discussion about some longer-term changes we are considering for the aura system.

DISCLAIMER: These notes are for addon authors and as such are focused specifically on addon security changes only. Changes planned for other parts of the game (UI or otherwise) are not included here.


=== Coming in 12.0.5 PTR 1 ===
=== Numeric Formatting ===
*We have added three new Lua object types for numeric formatting: AbbreviatedNumberFormatter, NumericRuleFormatter, and SecondsFormatter. These types can be supplied with secret numbers through the Format functions on duration objects.
*We're considering adjusting the various "display count" APIs (eg. C_Spell.GetSpellDisplayCount) to accept formatter objects, but this would be a breaking change (let us know your thoughts).

=== Spell & Item Charge APIs ===
*The following APIs will now return a zero-span duration object when the queried spell is at maximum charges: C_SpellBook.GetSpellBookItemChargeDuration, C_Spell.GetSpellChargeDuration, C_ActionBar.GetActionChargeDuration.

=== Duration Objects ===
*DurationObject objects that measure a zero-span are now considered fully elapsed.

=== Auras ===
*The isHelpful, isHarmful, isRaid, isNameplateOnly, and isFromPlayerOrPlayerPet booleans on aura data tables are no longer secret.

=== Transmog ===
*Added GetTransmogOutfitIndex to the restricted environment. Values returned from this can be used with the new /outfit slash command.

=== Lua Documentation ===
*Added a new Predicates table to out Lua API documentation, which will provide a description of the restrictions on each API.

=== Misc. ===
*The Ambiguate function now accepts secrets from addons.
*Added a Cooldown:SetCountdownMillisecondsThreshold(seconds) API. When a cooldown frame is rendering a time below this number of seconds, it will be displayed as a decimal value with one decimal place (e.g. "8.7").
*String formatting APIs no longer honor field width modifiers for secret string values (e.g. the "%.5s" format will no longer truncate a secret string).
*The UnitSpellTargetName API now only returns names for player units.

=== Bug fixes ===
The C_EncounterEvents.GetEventSound API no longer errors when called.


=== Coming in upcoming 12.0.5 PTRs ===
=== Misc. ===
*The UnitTokenFromGUID API (and various others) will no longer return arena, nameplate, boss, party, raid, or target-of-target unit tokens when unit identities are secret.
*UnitTokenNamePlate APIs will no longer accept party, raid, or target-of-target unit tokens.
*Addon execution throttles will no longer apply while the PLAYER_LOGOUT and ADDONS_UNLOADING events are being processed.


=== Future Plans ===

While we have a variety of plans for future patches (12.0.7 and beyond), including many more quality-of-life fixes for addon developers, we wanted to take a moment to talk about one area in particular that we are putting a lot of thought into: Auras (particularly of the Private variety).

We created the Private Aura system back in 10.1 as a means to prevent addons from automating certain very specific fight mechanics. In some ways Private Auras can be viewed as the beginning of our experimentation with adjusting addon capabilities, and while they certainly had their issues, for the most part they served their purpose (albeit in a rather heavy-handed way). When we started developing the Secret Value system, we had hoped (planned even) to be able to essentially retire the Private Aura system and replace it with just secrets.

Unfortunately, as Midnight Alpha & Beta progressed it became clear that relying on Secret Values alone was not going to be enough to prevent addon automation involving auras. And so, we ended up having to go in almost the exact opposite direction: we made MOST encounter debuffs private auras rather than just a select few. While this approach gave us the security we needed for Midnight Season 1, it also came with some significant downsides. Our own private aura displays don't currently have full parity with normal auras, and they aren’t supported in nameplates. On top of that they also require our encounter designers to be very diligent about flagging almost every encounter debuff as private, which is cumbersome and very easy to get wrong.

All this is to say that we are not happy with the current state of auras as they pertain to addons, and we are planning to make some large changes to them. We don't have a hard target yet for when this rework will happen, but just to ease your minds a little it definitely will NOT be in 12.0.5 or 12.0.7. What shape this new aura system will take is also nowhere near decided yet so we won't have any specifics for a while yet, but the overarching goals can be summed up as:

* Auras need to be more secure than they currently are (with less upkeep for designers).
* Auras still need to be customizable and displayable by addons.
* And then as a bonus goal we would like auras to be more performant for addons.

We will be consulting with addon developers as we start to plan out work on this new system, so don't worry about this being dropped on you out of the blue. We just wanted to give you an idea of where our heads are at, so it doesn't come as a surprise later.

Midnight 12.0.5 PTR Changes Episode 1: The Secret Menace

Hello again from Blizzard! With 12.0.5 PTR slated to start today, here is the list of addon API changes you can expect to see in next couple builds, followed by a discussion about some longer-term changes we are considering for the aura system.

DISCLAIMER: These notes are for addon authors and as such are focused specifically on addon security changes only. Changes planned for other parts of the game (UI or otherwise) are not included here.


=== Coming in 12.0.5 PTR 1 ===
=== Numeric Formatting ===
*We have added three new Lua object types for numeric formatting: AbbreviatedNumberFormatter, NumericRuleFormatter, and SecondsFormatter. These types can be supplied with secret numbers through the Format functions on duration objects.
*We're considering adjusting the various "display count" APIs (eg. C_Spell.GetSpellDisplayCount) to accept formatter objects, but this would be a breaking change (let us know your thoughts).

=== Spell & Item Charge APIs ===
*The following APIs will now return a zero-span duration object when the queried spell is at maximum charges: C_SpellBook.GetSpellBookItemChargeDuration, C_Spell.GetSpellChargeDuration, C_ActionBar.GetActionChargeDuration.

=== Duration Objects ===
*DurationObject objects that measure a zero-span are now considered fully elapsed.

=== Auras ===
*The isHelpful, isHarmful, isRaid, isNameplateOnly, and isFromPlayerOrPlayerPet booleans on aura data tables are no longer secret.

=== Transmog ===
*Added GetTransmogOutfitIndex to the restricted environment. Values returned from this can be used with the new /outfit slash command.

=== Lua Documentation ===
*Added a new Predicates table to out Lua API documentation, which will provide a description of the restrictions on each API.

=== Misc. ===
*The Ambiguate function now accepts secrets from addons.
*Added a Cooldown:SetCountdownMillisecondsThreshold(seconds) API. When a cooldown frame is rendering a time below this number of seconds, it will be displayed as a decimal value with one decimal place (e.g. "8.7").
*String formatting APIs no longer honor field width modifiers for secret string values (e.g. the "%.5s" format will no longer truncate a secret string).
*The UnitSpellTargetName API now only returns names for player units.

=== Bug fixes ===
The C_EncounterEvents.GetEventSound API no longer errors when called.


=== Coming in upcoming 12.0.5 PTRs ===
=== Misc. ===
*The UnitTokenFromGUID API (and various others) will no longer return arena, nameplate, boss, party, raid, or target-of-target unit tokens when unit identities are secret.
*UnitTokenNamePlate APIs will no longer accept party, raid, or target-of-target unit tokens.
*Addon execution throttles will no longer apply while the PLAYER_LOGOUT and ADDONS_UNLOADING events are being processed.


=== Future Plans ===

While we have a variety of plans for future patches (12.0.7 and beyond), including many more quality-of-life fixes for addon developers, we wanted to take a moment to talk about one area in particular that we are putting a lot of thought into: Auras (particularly of the Private variety).

We created the Private Aura system back in 10.1 as a means to prevent addons from automating certain very specific fight mechanics. In some ways Private Auras can be viewed as the beginning of our experimentation with adjusting addon capabilities, and while they certainly had their issues, for the most part they served their purpose (albeit in a rather heavy-handed way). When we started developing the Secret Value system, we had hoped (planned even) to be able to essentially retire the Private Aura system and replace it with just secrets.

Unfortunately, as Midnight Alpha & Beta progressed it became clear that relying on Secret Values alone was not going to be enough to prevent addon automation involving auras. And so, we ended up having to go in almost the exact opposite direction: we made MOST encounter debuffs private auras rather than just a select few. While this approach gave us the security we needed for Midnight Season 1, it also came with some significant downsides. Our own private aura displays don't currently have full parity with normal auras, and they aren’t supported in nameplates. On top of that they also require our encounter designers to be very diligent about flagging almost every encounter debuff as private, which is cumbersome and very easy to get wrong.

All this is to say that we are not happy with the current state of auras as they pertain to addons, and we are planning to make some large changes to them. We don't have a hard target yet for when this rework will happen, but just to ease your minds a little it definitely will NOT be in 12.0.5 or 12.0.7. What shape this new aura system will take is also nowhere near decided yet so we won't have any specifics for a while yet, but the overarching goals can be summed up as:

* Auras need to be more secure than they currently are (with less upkeep for designers).
* Auras still need to be customizable and displayable by addons.
* And then as a bonus goal we would like auras to be more performant for addons.

We will be consulting with addon developers as we start to plan out work on this new system, so don't worry about this being dropped on you out of the blue. We just wanted to give you an idea of where our heads are at, so it doesn't come as a surprise later.

Midnight 12.0.7 and Classic PTR Changes I

Hello again from Blizzard! With 12.0.7 PTR starting up soon, here is a list of the addon API changes you can expect to see.

DISCLAIMER: These notes are for addon authors and as such are focused specifically on addon-facing API and security changes only. Changes planned for other parts of the game (UI or otherwise) are not included here.


=== Coming in 12.0.7 PTR 1 ===
=== Tooltip Money Display ===
* Added a new GameTooltip_AddMoneyLine API, which uses embedded atlases to render money (via a new MoneyFormatter utility) rather than MoneyFrame.
** Addons are advised to use the new API to avoid issues with secret values in tooltips.
** All usages of SetTooltipMoney in our code have been removed.

=== Unit Identity ===
* APIs that restrict certain unit token types (such as UnitGUID, C_UnitAuras.GetAuraDataByIndex, and health/power APIs when called with PvP-restricted tokens) will no longer raise Lua errors when fed an unsupported token. They will instead return nil or an appropriate default value.

=== Encounter Events ===
* ENCOUNTER_END now includes an additional payload: a list of EncounterUnitStatus tables for all boss units that were engaged during the encounter.
** Each entry contains the unit's creatureID, creatureName, and remainingHealthPercent (as non-secrets) at the time they were killed/disengaged (or, when the encounter ended).
* C_EncounterEvents now allows configuration of different colors for text warnings and timeline events.
** Additionally, a custom color can be defined for when a timeline event reaches the 5 seconds remaining mark, signaled via ENCOUNTER_TIMELINE_EVENT_COLOR_CHANGED.
* C_EncounterEvents now accepts alpha values for its color APIs.

=== File Asset APIs ===
* Added a new C_UIFileAsset namespace with the following APIs to help addons validate font and texture paths before using them:
** C_UIFileAsset.GetFileID(asset) - returns the numeric file ID for a given path or file ID, or nil if the asset is not known to the client.
** C_UIFileAsset.IsKnownFile(asset) - returns true if the asset is present in the shipped client data or is a known local loose file.
** C_UIFileAsset.IsLooseFile(asset) - returns true if the asset is a locally known loose (non-shipped) file.

=== Profiling APIs ===
* The following profiling APIs have been made available to addons again: GetEventCPUUsage, GetFunctionCPUUsage, and GetScriptCPUUsage.

=== Gamepad / SimulateMouse ===
* SimulateMouse APIs (eg. SimulateMouseDown, SimulateMouseClick) no longer carry taint when used.
** In order to allow them to run taint-free, these APIs have been restricted to only function when all current mouse foci are not forbidden, locked down, script inaccessible, or protected frames (while in combat).
** They are still restricted to only being used via a gamepad action.

=== Debug APIs ===
* debugstack and debuglocals will now return secret values if the current function — or any caller up the stack — has accessed a secret value.

=== Misc ===
* Fixed various issues with secrets causing issues when present in regions displayed in scrollboxes.
* C_ScenarioInfo.GetUnitCriteriaProgressValues now returns its second value (a percentage) in the range [0, 1] rather than [0, 100].
* The default script error reporter dialog will no longer display a blank frame if there are non-printable characters such as null bytes in the text.
* Chat events for currency, honor, loot, money, reputation, and XP gains are no longer secret.
* Support has been added for per-directive conditionals in addon toc files (e.g. ## Dep: Addon_X [AllowLoadGameType classic]).
* FontInstance:SetFont has more informative error messaging when supplied invalid font flag names.


=== Coming in upcoming Classic PTR builds ===
* Most secret-related fields have been removed from the autogenerated Lua API documentation in Classic builds.
** Fields such as SecretArguments, ConditionalSecret, SecretPayloads, and secret predicate documentation will no longer appear in the Classic API docs, since these concepts don't apply there.
* The RemoveRaidTargets API has been added to Classic.
* Various APIs for obtaining missing health and powers that operate on CurveObjectBase (and UnitHealPredictionCalculator) have been added to Classic.
* Minimap pings are no longer restricted in Classic.
* Raid target marker throttles are significantly relaxed in Classic.
* Macro-initiated chat and chat channel commands are no longer restricted in Classic.
* APIs that take limited subsets of unit tokens from tainted code are no longer restricted in Classic (this doesn't apply to UnitTokenNameplate).


=== 2026-05-28 ===
Midnight 12.0.7 PTR Changes II

Hello again from Blizzard! Today's 12.0.7 PTR build is our first 12.0.7 RC (there may be more), so here is a list of the addon API changes in this build, along with a review of some of the changes that went into recent 12.0.7 PTR builds since our last update. And then finally a short note with some timeline info about the upcoming Aura refactor.

DISCLAIMER: These notes are for addon authors and as such are focused specifically on addon-facing API and security changes only. Changes planned for other parts of the game (UI or otherwise) are not included here.


=== New in 12.0.7 RC 1 ===
* Added a new "set-unmarked" option for the raidtarget secure action that will set a raid marker on the player's target if they don't currently have a marker on them.
** The /tm command now supports this same behavior by using ~ preceding the marker index (e.g. /tm ~4).
* The following C_MythicPlus APIs now return CalendarTime structs instead of MythicPlusDate structs: C_MythicPlus.GetRunHistory, C_MythicPlus.GetWeeklyBestForMap, and C_MythicPlus.GetSeasonBestForMap.
* The GROUP_FORMED event now gets correctly sent when the player joins a follower dungeon or delve on their own.
* The isFromPlayerOrPlayerPet bool in AuraData structs is now set to true if the aura came from a player-controlled vehicle.
* Addons are now allowed to call C_UnitAuras.AddPrivateAuraAppliedSound during an active M+ as long as the player isn't in combat.
* Fixed a bug that caused secret value errors in the Frame:SetFrameStrata API (often in chat-related code).


=== Changes in other recent 12.0.7 PTR builds ===
* The identity of units with the "npc" unit token are no longer secret when the player is in an active item interaction with them.
* The BNInviteFriend API has been migrated to C_BattleNet.InviteFriend (and an occasions secrets-related Lua error was fixed as a result).
* Added a new DurationTextBinding script object type. This allows addons to bind a duration value directly to a font string, causing the string to update automatically based on the duration.

Example usage:

local duration = C_DurationUtil.CreateDuration();
duration:SetTimeSpan(GetTime() - 10, GetTime() + 20);
local secondsFormatter = C_StringUtil.CreateSecondsFormatter();
secondsFormatter:SetDefaultAbbreviation(Enum.SecondsFormatterAbbreviation.OneLetter);
secondsFormatter:SetStripIntervalWhitespace(Enum.SecondsFormatterIntervalWhitespace.Strip);
secondsFormatter:SetMillisecondsThreshold(5);

local binding = C_DurationUtil.CreateDurationTextBinding();
binding:SetFontString(PlayerName);
binding:SetDuration(duration);
binding:SetFormatter(secondsFormatter);
binding:SetExpiredText("Done!");
binding:SetZeroDurationText("");
binding:SetEnabled(true);



=== Timeline for the Aura Refactor ===
As previously mentioned in past posts, we are working on a refactor of how we expose auras to addons. The high level goal of this refactor is to make auras much more secure while still allowing addons to create their own filtered aura displays and customize the way they are displayed. We are not quite ready to announce the technical details but are ready to tell you that we are currently targeting the 12.1.0 patch for these changes (subject to change as needed of course). We will be giving a full technical breakdown of the changes once they are solidified and reaching out to gather thoughts and feedback from several of you individually well before then, so stay tuned!

=== Tooltip Money Display ===
* Added a new GameTooltip_AddMoneyLine API, which uses embedded atlases to render money (via a new MoneyFormatter utility) rather than MoneyFrame.
** Addons are advised to use the new API to avoid issues with secret values in tooltips.
** All usages of SetTooltipMoney in our code have been removed.

=== Unit Identity ===
* APIs that restrict certain unit token types (such as UnitGUID, C_UnitAuras.GetAuraDataByIndex, and health/power APIs when called with PvP-restricted tokens) will no longer raise Lua errors when fed an unsupported token. They will instead return nil or an appropriate default value.

=== Encounter Events ===
* ENCOUNTER_END now includes an additional payload: a list of EncounterUnitStatus tables for all boss units that were engaged during the encounter.
** Each entry contains the unit's creatureID, creatureName, and remainingHealthPercent (as non-secrets) at the time they were killed/disengaged (or, when the encounter ended).
* C_EncounterEvents now allows configuration of different colors for text warnings and timeline events.
** Additionally, a custom color can be defined for when a timeline event reaches the 5 seconds remaining mark, signaled via ENCOUNTER_TIMELINE_EVENT_COLOR_CHANGED.
* C_EncounterEvents now accepts alpha values for its color APIs.

=== File Asset APIs ===
* Added a new C_UIFileAsset namespace with the following APIs to help addons validate font and texture paths before using them:
** C_UIFileAsset.GetFileID(asset) - returns the numeric file ID for a given path or file ID, or nil if the asset is not known to the client.
** C_UIFileAsset.IsKnownFile(asset) - returns true if the asset is present in the shipped client data or is a known local loose file.
** C_UIFileAsset.IsLooseFile(asset) - returns true if the asset is a locally known loose (non-shipped) file.

=== Profiling APIs ===
* The following profiling APIs have been made available to addons again: GetEventCPUUsage, GetFunctionCPUUsage, and GetScriptCPUUsage.

* SimulateMouse APIs (eg. SimulateMouseDown, SimulateMouseClick) no longer carry taint when used.
** In order to allow them to run taint-free, these APIs have been restricted to only function when all current mouse foci are not forbidden, locked down, script inaccessible, or protected frames (while in combat).
** They are still restricted to only being used via a gamepad action.

=== Debug APIs ===
* debugstack and debuglocals will now return secret values if the current function — or any caller up the stack — has accessed a secret value.

=== Misc ===
* Fixed various issues with secrets causing issues when present in regions displayed in scrollboxes.
* C_ScenarioInfo.GetUnitCriteriaProgressValues now returns its second value (a percentage) in the range [0, 1] rather than [0, 100].
* The default script error reporter dialog will no longer display a blank frame if there are non-printable characters such as null bytes in the text.
* Chat events for currency, honor, loot, money, reputation, and XP gains are no longer secret.

Patch 9.2.5 API changes

== Summary ==
* Significant modifications were made to the UnitPopup menu system. See UnitPopup Changes for more information.
* Added various APIs relating to cross-faction player co-operation.
* Added Region:GetSourceLocation() which returns the script name and line where a Region was created.
* Added a new reusable system for dropdowns that configure list filters.
* Added a new player name autocompletion flag - AUTO_COMPLETE_RECENT_PLAYER.
* The GetPlayerAuraBySpellID() API no longer returns information about hidden auras.
* (9.2.0) Added isFullUpdate and updatedAuras parameters to UNIT_AURA.[https://www.bluetracker.gg/wow/topic/us-en/1205007-new-unit_aura-processing-optimizations/]
Enums
* Changed the casing of various LFG enumerations; usages of "Lfg" have been renamed to the fully-uppercase "LFG". The old names are deprecated.
* Added new enums for calendar events and invites. The old global constants have been deprecated.
* Added a new enum for LFG filter flags. The old global constants are deprecated.

== UnitPopup Changes ==
[Warning: Secure Execution and Tainting]
* Modifying UnitPopup menus as described below will taint and break other secure actions in the same menu.

The UnitPopup system has been reworked to cut down on the differences between the Retail and Classic clients. This is a breaking change and may require alterations to addons that were previously modifying global tables to add, remove, or modify buttons on right-click menus for units.

To create a new button to be displayed on unit menus create a mixin that derives from UnitPopupButtonBaseMixin.


local CustomMenuButtonMixin = CreateFromMixins(UnitPopupButtonBaseMixin)

function CustomMenuButtonMixin:GetText() return "My Button" end
function CustomMenuButtonMixin:OnClick() print("Clicked!") end


To then add this button to a menu pre-hook the appropriate GetMenuButtons() method on each menu table that you want to modify. This can also be used to remove or re-order existing buttons within the same menu.


-- This example will modify the "Target" unit menu and add the custom button
-- from the example above as the first button in its list.

local GetTargetMenuButtons = UnitPopupMenuTarget.GetMenuButtons

function UnitPopupMenuTarget:GetMenuButtons()
    local buttons = GetTargetMenuButtons(self)
    table.insert(buttons, 1, CustomMenuButtonMixin)
    return buttons
end


The list of all unit menu tables can be found split across two files; UnitPopupSharedMenus.lua for menus shared between all client flavors, and UnitPopupMenus.lua for per-client customizations.

== UnitPopup Changes ==
[Warning: Secure Execution and Tainting]
* Modifying UnitPopup menus as described below will taint and break other secure actions in the same menu.

The UnitPopup system has been reworked to cut down on the differences between the Retail and Classic clients. This is a breaking change and may require alterations to addons that were previously modifying global tables to add, remove, or modify buttons on right-click menus for units.

To create a new button to be displayed on unit menus create a mixin that derives from UnitPopupButtonBaseMixin.

```lua
local CustomMenuButtonMixin = CreateFromMixins(UnitPopupButtonBaseMixin)

function CustomMenuButtonMixin:GetText() return "My Button" end
function CustomMenuButtonMixin:OnClick() print("Clicked!") end
```

To then add this button to a menu pre-hook the appropriate GetMenuButtons() method on each menu table that you want to modify. This can also be used to remove or re-order existing buttons within the same menu.

```lua
-- This example will modify the "Target" unit menu and add the custom button
-- from the example above as the first button in its list.

local GetTargetMenuButtons = UnitPopupMenuTarget.GetMenuButtons

function UnitPopupMenuTarget:GetMenuButtons()
    local buttons = GetTargetMenuButtons(self)
    table.insert(buttons, 1, CustomMenuButtonMixin)
    return buttons
end
```

The list of all unit menu tables can be found split across two files; UnitPopupSharedMenus.lua for menus shared between all client flavors, and UnitPopupMenus.lua for per-client customizations.
